--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### SearchProvider

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/core/search-provider
Description: Interface contract for pluggable search providers in DataFn.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The `SearchProvider` interface defines the contract that any search backend must implement to integrate with DataFn's client and server search routing. It is exported from `@datafn/core`.

```typescript
import type { SearchProvider } from "@datafn/core";
```

## Interface

```typescript
interface SearchProvider {
  readonly name: string;
  search(params: SearchParams): Promise<string[]>;
  searchAll?(params: SearchAllParams): Promise<Array<{ resource: string; id: string; score: number }>>;
  updateIndices(params: UpdateIndicesParams): Promise<void>;
  clearIndices?(resource: string): Promise<void>;
  initialize?(config: InitializeConfig): Promise<void>;
  dispose?(): Promise<void>;
}
```

## Required Members

### `name`

```typescript
readonly name: string;
```

Unique identifier for the provider. Used in logs and diagnostics.

### `search`

```typescript
search(params: {
  resource: string;
  query: string;
  type?: "fullText" | "semantic";
  fields?: string[];
  limit?: number;
  prefix?: boolean;
  fuzzy?: boolean | number;
  fieldBoosts?: Record<string, number>;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}): Promise<string[]>;
```

Search a single resource. Returns an array of matching record IDs (as strings), ordered by relevance.

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `string` | Resource name to search. |
| `query` | `string` | Search text. |
| `type` | `"fullText" \| "semantic"` | Search mode. Defaults to `"fullText"`. |
| `fields` | `string[]` | Optional subset of indexed fields to search. |
| `limit` | `number` | Maximum number of results. |
| `prefix` | `boolean` | Enable prefix token matching. |
| `fuzzy` | `boolean \| number` | Enable fuzzy matching. A number sets the tolerance/distance. |
| `fieldBoosts` | `Record<string, number>` | Per-field relevance weights. Values must be finite positive numbers. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | Optional abort signal for cancellation. |

### `updateIndices`

```typescript
updateIndices(params: {
  resource: string;
  records: Record<string, unknown>[];
  operation: "upsert" | "delete";
}): Promise<void>;
```

Called by DataFn after mutations to keep the search index current.

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `resource` | `string` | Resource being updated. |
| `records` | `Record<string, unknown>[]` | Records to index or remove. Each record includes an `id` field. |
| `operation` | `"upsert" \| "delete"` | Whether to add/update or remove records from the index. |

## Optional Members

### `clearIndices`

```typescript
clearIndices?(resource: string): Promise<void>;
```

Clears all indexed documents for one resource before DataFn performs a full rebuild. Providers that persist index data should implement this method. DataFn requires it when an existing index fingerprint changes so deleted documents cannot survive a schema, field, provider, or `searchIndexVersion` change. The `@searchfn/datafn-provider` bridge delegates it to the SearchFn adapter's `clear(resource)` method.

### `searchAll`

```typescript
searchAll?(params: {
  query: string;
  resources?: string[];
  fields?: string[];
  limit?: number;
  limitPerResource?: number;
  prefix?: boolean;
  fuzzy?: boolean | number;
  fieldBoosts?: Record<string, number>;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}): Promise<Array<{ resource: string; id: string; score: number }>>;
```

Cross-resource search. Returns ranked results across multiple resources. Used by `client.search()`.

If not implemented, DataFn falls back to calling `search()` per resource and merging results by score.

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `string` | Search text. |
| `resources` | `string[]` | Resources to search. Omit to search all. |
| `fields` | `string[]` | Optional subset of indexed fields. |
| `limit` | `number` | Maximum total results. |
| `limitPerResource` | `number` | Maximum results per resource. |
| `prefix` | `boolean` | Enable prefix token matching. |
| `fuzzy` | `boolean \| number` | Enable fuzzy matching. |
| `fieldBoosts` | `Record<string, number>` | Per-field relevance weights. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | Optional abort signal for cancellation. |

### `initialize`

```typescript
initialize?(config: {
  resources: Array<{ name: string; searchFields: string[] }>;
}): Promise<void>;
```

Called once at client startup with resource/searchField mappings derived from the schema. Use this to set up indices, allocate storage, or pre-warm caches.

### `dispose`

```typescript
dispose?(): Promise<void>;
```

Called when the client is destroyed. Use this to release resources, close connections, or flush pending writes.

## Implementing a Custom Provider

```typescript
import type { SearchProvider } from "@datafn/core";

const myProvider: SearchProvider = {
  name: "my-custom-search",

  async search({ resource, query, prefix, fuzzy, fieldBoosts, limit }) {
    // Query your search backend and return matching IDs
    const results = await mySearchBackend.query(resource, query, { prefix, fuzzy, fieldBoosts });
    return results.slice(0, limit).map((r) => r.id);
  },

  async updateIndices({ resource, records, operation }) {
    if (operation === "upsert") {
      await mySearchBackend.index(resource, records);
    } else {
      await mySearchBackend.remove(resource, records.map((r) => r.id));
    }
  },

  async initialize({ resources }) {
    for (const { name, searchFields } of resources) {
      await mySearchBackend.ensureIndex(name, searchFields);
    }
  },

  async dispose() {
    await mySearchBackend.close();
  },
};
```

## Pre-Built Providers

The `@searchfn/datafn-provider` package bridges any [SearchFn](/docs/dfql/search#setting-up-a-search-provider) adapter into the `SearchProvider` interface:

```typescript
import { createSearchProvider } from "@searchfn/datafn-provider";
import { IndexedDbAdapter } from "@searchfn/adapter-indexeddb";

const provider = createSearchProvider(
  new IndexedDbAdapter({ dbName: "my-app-search" }),
  { resourceFields: { tasks: ["title", "description"] } },
);
```

See [Search — Setting Up a Search Provider](/docs/dfql/search#setting-up-a-search-provider) for the full setup guide.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Temporal

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/core/temporal
Description: Timezone-aware temporal types, builders, and resolution helpers from @datafn/core.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

`@datafn/core` exports the temporal type system, the `time` clause builder, and a set of resolution helpers. These are isomorphic — the client and server import the same functions. For the conceptual guide, see [DFQL Temporal](/docs/dfql/temporal).

## Types

```typescript
type DatafnTemporalScale = "hour" | "day" | "week" | "month" | "quarter" | "year";
type DatafnTemporalStorage = "unix-ms" | "unix-s" | "date" | "iso";

type DatafnTemporalRangeInput = { start: string | number | Date; end: string | number | Date };
type DatafnTemporalPeriodInput = { scale: DatafnTemporalScale; at?: string | number | Date };
type DatafnTemporalGroupInput = {
  scale: DatafnTemporalScale;
  alias?: string;
  output?: DatafnTemporalStorage;
  weekStartsOn?: number;
};

type DatafnTemporalClause = {
  field: string;
  timezone?: string;
  storage?: DatafnTemporalStorage;
  weekStartsOn?: number;
  range?: DatafnTemporalRangeInput;
  period?: DatafnTemporalPeriodInput;
  groupBy?: DatafnTemporalGroupInput;
};

type DatafnTemporalConfig = {
  timezone?: string | (() => string | undefined);
  timezoneResolver?: DatafnTemporalTimezoneResolver;
  weekStartsOn?: number;
};

type DatafnTemporalTimezoneResolver = (input: {
  instant: number;
  field: string;
  resource?: string;
  record?: Record<string, unknown>;
  scale?: DatafnTemporalScale;
}) => string | undefined;

type DatafnTimezoneChangeRecord = {
  id: string;
  timezone: string;
  effectiveFrom: number;
  recordedAt: number;
  source?: string;
};
```

## `time` / `temporal`

Clause builders. `temporal` is an alias for `time`.

```typescript
import { time } from "@datafn/core";

time.range(field, { start, end }, options?);
time.between(field, start, end, options?);
time.period(field, { scale, at? }, options?);
time.group(field, scale, options?);            // options: { alias?, output?, timezone?, storage?, weekStartsOn? }

time.hour(field, at?, options?);
time.day(field, at?, options?);
time.week(field, at?, options?);
time.month(field, at?, options?);
time.quarter(field, at?, options?);
time.year(field, at?, options?);

time.groupByHour(field, options?);
time.groupByDay(field, options?);
time.groupByWeek(field, options?);
time.groupByMonth(field, options?);
time.groupByQuarter(field, options?);
time.groupByYear(field, options?);
```

`options` accepts the non-`field` members of `DatafnTemporalClause` (`timezone`, `storage`, `weekStartsOn`). Group helpers additionally accept `alias` and `output`.

## Query Normalization

| Function | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `normalizeTemporalQuery` | `<T>(query: T, config?: DatafnTemporalConfig) => T` | Compiles `period`/`range` clauses into `$gte`/`$lte` filters, retains `groupBy` clauses, and merges generated filters with any existing `filters` using `$and`. |
| `getTemporalClauses` | `(query) => DatafnTemporalClause[]` | Returns the query's temporal clauses as an array. |
| `hasTemporalGrouping` | `(query) => boolean` | `true` when any clause has a `groupBy`. |
| `getTemporalGroups` | `(query, config?) => DatafnResolvedTemporalGroup[]` | Resolved grouping descriptors (alias defaults to `${field}_${scale}`, `output` defaults to `"iso"`, `weekStartsOn` defaults to `1`). |
| `getTemporalGroupAliases` | `(query) => Set<string>` | The set of group aliases (valid as sort/having keys and in authz). |

```typescript
import { normalizeTemporalQuery, time } from "@datafn/core";

normalizeTemporalQuery({
  resource: "session",
  version: 1,
  filters: { status: "done" },
  temporal: time.month("startedAt", instant, { timezone: "Asia/Kolkata" }),
});
// => { resource, version, filters: { $and: [{ status: "done" }, { startedAt: { $gte, $lte } }] } }
```

## Value Resolution

| Function | Description |
|---|---|
| `resolveTemporalBucketValue(record, group)` | The bucket key for a record under a resolved group. |
| `resolveTemporalBucketKey(input, config?)` | The bucket key for an explicit `DatafnTemporalBucketInput`. |
| `resolveTemporalPeriodRange(period, timezone?, weekStartsOn?)` | `{ start, end }` epoch-ms for a calendar period. |
| `startOfTemporalPeriod(value, scale, timezone?, weekStartsOn?)` | Period start instant (epoch-ms). |
| `addTemporalPeriod(periodStartMs, scale, timezone?)` | Advance one period. |
| `resolveTemporalLocalTime(input, timezone?)` | Resolve a `{ year, month, day, ... }` local time to epoch-ms. |
| `toTemporalStorageValue(ms, storage?)` | Convert epoch-ms to the configured storage format. |
| `resolveTemporalInputMs(value, storage?)` | Parse a stored value into epoch-ms. |

## Timezone Registry

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_RESOURCE_NAME` | `"datafnTimezoneChange"` — the built-in registry resource name. |
| `TIMEZONE_CHANGE_ID_PREFIX` | `"timezoneChange"` — id prefix for registry records. |
| `timezoneChangeId(effectiveFrom, timezone, suffix?)` | Build a deterministic registry record id. |
| `createTimezoneResolver(records, options?)` | Build a `DatafnTemporalTimezoneResolver` from registry records, resolving the most recent zone effective at each instant. |
| `ensureBuiltinTemporal(schema)` | Append (or validate) the `datafnTimezoneChange` resource. Called automatically by the client, server, and CLI codegen. |

## Plugin

```typescript
createTemporalPlugin(config?: DatafnTemporalConfig): DatafnPlugin
```

Returns a `runsOn: ["client", "server"]` plugin whose `beforeQuery` hook runs `normalizeTemporalQuery` over each query (including batch arrays) with the supplied configuration.

## Related

- [DFQL Temporal](/docs/dfql/temporal) — conceptual guide.
- [`client.temporal` reference](/docs/reference/client/temporal) — user-timezone management.

### Core Types

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/core/types
Description: Type definitions exported by @datafn/core.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Capability Types

```typescript
type SimpleCapability = "timestamps" | "audit" | "trash" | "archivable";

type AccessLevel = "viewer" | "editor" | "owner";

type ShareableCapability = {
  shareable: {
    levels: AccessLevel[];
    default: "private" | "shared";
  };
};

type CapabilityEntry = SimpleCapability | ShareableCapability;

type SchemaCapabilities = CapabilityEntry[];

type ResourceCapabilities = CapabilityEntry[] | { exclude: SimpleCapability[] };

type RelationSimpleCapability = "timestamps" | "audit";
```

## DatafnSchema

```typescript
type DatafnSchema = {
  capabilities?: SchemaCapabilities;
  resources: DatafnResourceSchema[];
  relations?: DatafnRelationSchema[];
  relationIntegrity?: DatafnRelationIntegrityMode;
  namespaced?: boolean;
};

type DatafnRelationIntegrityMode = "application" | "database";
```

`relationIntegrity` defaults to `"application"`. The removed `"hybrid"` mode is rejected by `validateSchema`.

## DatafnResourceSchema

```typescript
type DatafnResourceSchema = {
  name: string;
  version: number;
  idPrefix?: string;
  isRemoteOnly?: boolean;
  capabilities?: ResourceCapabilities;
  fields: DatafnFieldSchema[];
  indices?:
    | { base?: string[]; search?: string[]; vector?: string[] }
    | string[];
  permissions?: DatafnPermissionsPolicy;
};
```

## DatafnFieldSchema

```typescript
type DatafnFieldSchema = {
  name: string;
  type: "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "object" | "array" | "date" | "file" | "json";
  required: boolean;
  nullable?: boolean;
  readonly?: boolean;
  default?: unknown;
  enum?: unknown[];
  min?: number;
  max?: number;
  minLength?: number;
  maxLength?: number;
  pattern?: string;
  unique?: boolean | string;
  encrypt?: boolean;
  volatile?: boolean;
};
```

## DatafnRelationSchema

```typescript
type DatafnRelationSchema = {
  from: string | readonly string[];
  to: string | readonly string[];
  type: "one-many" | "many-one" | "many-many" | "htree";
  relation?: string;
  inverse?: string;
  cache?: boolean;
  metadata?: Array<{
    name: string;
    type: "string" | "number" | "boolean" | "date" | "object" | "json";
  }>;
  fkField?: string;
  fkResourceField?: string;
  pathField?: string;
  joinTable?: string;
  joinColumns?: { from: string; to: string };
  capabilities?: RelationSimpleCapability[];
  integrity?: DatafnRelationIntegrityMode;
  onDelete?: DatafnRelationDeletePolicies;
};

type DatafnRelationDeletePolicy = "restrict" | "cascade" | "setNull" | "detach";
type DatafnRelationDeletePolicies =
  | DatafnRelationDeletePolicy
  | { from?: DatafnRelationDeletePolicy; to?: DatafnRelationDeletePolicy };
```

An array `from`/`to` declares a [polymorphic](/docs/dfql/schema/relations#polymorphic-relations) endpoint; `fkResourceField` names the discriminator column for polymorphic FK sides. See [Relations](/docs/dfql/schema/relations) for `integrity` and `onDelete` semantics.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Envelopes Reference

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/envelopes
Description: Every DataFn response is a DatafnEnvelope. Here is the shape and the helpers.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## DatafnEnvelope&lt;T&gt;

A discriminated union over success and error:

```typescript
type DatafnEnvelope<T> =
  | { ok: true;  result: T }
  | { ok: false; error: DatafnError };

type DatafnError = {
  code: DatafnErrorCode;
  message: string;
  details?: { path: string; [key: string]: unknown };
};
```

Every HTTP route, every client method, every plugin hook returns this shape — it's the protocol's only carrier type.

## Why an envelope?

- **No exceptions over the wire.** All failures travel as data; you switch on `code`.
- **Composable.** A transaction's response is `DatafnEnvelope<{ results: DatafnEnvelope<...>[] }>` — failures at any depth surface as the same shape.
- **Type-safe.** A `if (env.ok)` narrows `env.result` automatically; the error branch narrows `env.error`.
- **Replay-friendly.** Stored envelopes can be replayed for idempotency without re-running the underlying operation.

## Constructors

```typescript
import { ok, err } from "@datafn/core";

ok({ data: [], hasMore: false });
// { ok: true, result: { data: [], hasMore: false } }

err("DFQL_INVALID", "Missing resource field");
// { ok: false, error: { code: "DFQL_INVALID", message: "Missing resource field", details: { path: "$" } } }

err("LIMIT_EXCEEDED", "Too many fields", { limit: 50, requested: 80 });
// { ok: false, error: { code: "LIMIT_EXCEEDED", message: "Too many fields", details: { limit: 50, requested: 80 } } }
```

`details` defaults to `{ path: "$" }` when not provided.

## Unwrapping

```typescript
import { unwrapEnvelope } from "@datafn/core";

const schema = unwrapEnvelope(validateSchema(input));
// → returns the result on success
// → throws the error on failure
```

Use `unwrapEnvelope` when you want exceptions in a code path you control (typically in startup code). Avoid it in request handlers — preserve the envelope and surface `error.code` to the caller.

## On the wire

A response is exactly the envelope, serialized as JSON, with `content-type: application/json`. HTTP status is `200 OK` for both success and "graceful" errors. The server only returns non-200 for transport-level problems (`503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` during shutdown, `429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` if a rate limit middleware is configured).

This matters for monitoring: a `4xx` rate doesn't indicate DataFn errors. To monitor envelope failures, look at `result.error.code` in the response body.

## Composing envelopes

When a route returns multiple results (e.g. batch queries, push results), each entry is itself an envelope:

```typescript
// POST /datafn/query  (batch body)
type BatchQueryResult = DatafnEnvelope<DatafnEnvelope<{ data: any[]; hasMore: boolean }>[]>;
```

The outer envelope reflects "did the route accept the request at all"; the inner envelopes reflect "did each query succeed individually". The same pattern is used by `/datafn/transact` step results.

## Idempotency cache

For `/datafn/mutation` (and `/datafn/push`), every successful envelope is cached against `clientId + mutationId`. A replay returns the cached envelope verbatim — same `serverSeq`, same `result.id`, no side effects. See [Idempotency](/docs/documentation/advanced/idempotency) for the cache semantics and TTL.

## Pattern: surfacing errors in the UI

```typescript
const env = await client.table("tasks").mutate({ operation: "insert", record: { title } });

if (env.ok) {
  toast.success(`Created ${env.result.id}`);
} else {
  switch (env.error.code) {
    case "DFQL_INVALID":
      form.setError(env.error.details?.path as string, { message: env.error.message });
      break;
    case "FORBIDDEN":
      toast.error("You don't have permission to do that.");
      break;
    case "TRANSPORT_ERROR":
      // The mutation was queued offline; nothing to do.
      break;
    default:
      toast.error(`Unexpected error: ${env.error.code}`);
  }
}
```



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Errors Reference

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/errors
Description: Canonical error code matrix: what each code means, what causes it, and how to fix it.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every DataFn server response uses the same envelope:

```typescript
type DatafnEnvelope<T> =
  | { ok: true; result: T }
  | { ok: false; error: DatafnError };

type DatafnError = {
  code: DatafnErrorCode;
  message: string;
  details?: { path: string; [key: string]: unknown };
};
```

When you see `ok: false`, route on `error.code` — it's the stable, machine-readable identifier. `error.message` and `error.details.path` carry human-readable context.

## Schema errors

These fire at server startup (during `validateSchema`) or when a schema is loaded by a client.

| Code | Common cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SCHEMA_INVALID` | Structural problems: too many resources/fields, duplicate names, unknown field referenced in an index. | Run `npx @datafn/cli validate --schema shared/schema.ts` locally — the error message names the offending path. |
| `INVALID_CAPABILITY` | A capability name in the array is not recognized (e.g. `"sharable"` instead of `"shareable"`). | Use one of the documented capabilities. See [Capabilities](/docs/documentation/capabilities). |
| `INVALID_CAPABILITY_CONFIG` | A capability config object is the wrong shape (e.g. `shareable: { defaultVisibility: "everyone" }`). | Check the capability's config contract in [Capabilities](/docs/documentation/capabilities). |
| `CAPABILITY_FIELD_COLLISION` | A field you declared has the same name as a capability-injected system field (e.g. declaring `createdAt` while `timestamps` is enabled). | Drop the conflicting field; capabilities own these names. See [System Fields](/docs/dfql/schema/system-fields). |
| `CAPABILITY_DEPENDENCY` | A capability requires another that isn't enabled (`shareable` depends on `audit`). | Add the dependency to the schema or remove the dependent capability. |

## DFQL errors

These fire on query, mutation, or transaction requests when the payload doesn't match the schema.

| Code | Common cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DFQL_INVALID` | Required field missing, value of wrong type, malformed filter, malformed cursor. | Inspect `error.details.path` — it pinpoints the bad subtree. |
| `DFQL_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE` | Resource name in the payload isn't in the schema. | Re-run codegen if you renamed/added a resource. |
| `DFQL_UNKNOWN_FIELD` | A field in `select`, `filters`, `sort`, or `record` isn't on the resource. | Same as above. |
| `DFQL_UNKNOWN_RELATION` | A relation path in `select` references an undeclared relation. | Add the relation to the schema or fix the path. |
| `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED` | A feature (operator, capability operation) is not supported by the current server build. | Common in cross-resource search without a `SearchProvider`. Configure the missing dependency. |
| `DFQL_ABORTED` | A step in `transact` aborted because a prior step failed. | Check the first non-`DFQL_ABORTED` error in `results`. |
| `DFQL_SHARE_SCOPE_INVALID` | `share` mutation with an invalid `scope` (must be `"record"` or `"resource"`). | Pass `scope: "record"` + `id`, or `scope: "resource"` (no id). |
| `DFQL_PRINCIPAL_INVALID` | `share` mutation with an empty `principalId`, both `principalId` and `userId`, or neither. | Pass one of them, non-empty. |
| `DFQL_CROSS_NS_SHARE_FORBIDDEN` | `share` mutation crossing namespaces with `crossNsShareable: false`. | Either flip the resource config or share within-namespace. |

## Authz and limits

| Code | Common cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FORBIDDEN` | `authorize()` returned `false`, field-level authz denied the action, or sharing rules rejected the principal. | Tighten or loosen `authorize` and the relevant `permissions` policy. See [Authorization](/docs/documentation/server/authorization). |
| `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | A request exceeded `limits.maxLimit`, `maxTransactSteps`, `maxPayloadBytes`, `maxBatchSize`, etc. | Lower the request or raise the limit. See [Server Setup](/docs/documentation/server/setup#limits). |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Mutation referenced an `id` that does not exist (or that the actor cannot see). | Check the id exists and that the actor has access. |
| `CONFLICT` | Insert with a colliding id, or an `if` guard that failed. | Use `merge` if you want upsert semantics. For guards, refresh the row and retry. |

## Runtime / infrastructure

| Code | Common cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `INTERNAL` | Unclassified server error (database connection, plugin throwing, etc.). | Check server logs; this code is never thrown intentionally. |
| `TRANSACTION_ROLLED_BACK` | A step in `transact` failed and the entire transaction was rolled back. | Inspect prior step error(s); the rollback itself is correct. |
| `TRANSPORT_ERROR` | Client-side network error (timeout, connection refused, DNS). Never returned by the server. | Surface to the user; retry with backoff. |

## Apple-only

These codes only surface on the Apple runtime when running with the iCloud sync backend or with the WebView bridge.

| Code | Common cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE` | WebView bridge isn't yet wired up. | Call `runtime.makeBridgeHost(...)` and inject the host script before triggering JS-side mutations. |
| `BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_MISMATCH` | The WebView is running an older bridge version than the host. | Rebuild the WebView bundle. |
| `BRIDGE_METHOD_UNSUPPORTED` | JS requested a host method the runtime doesn't expose. | Update DatafnAppleRuntime, or drop the call. |
| `NATIVE_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE` | Same as `BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE` but from native code. | See above. |
| `NATIVE_SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE` | Search index hasn't been built for the resource. | Trigger a `runtime.search.rebuild(...)`. |
| `NATIVE_SYNC_CONFLICT` | CoreData detected a conflict that the runtime couldn't resolve. | Inspect logs and adjust merge policy. |
| `SEARCH_INDEX_REBUILD_FAILED` | Disk full, permissions, or a search provider crash. | Check device storage; restart the runtime. |
| `ICLOUD_UNAVAILABLE` | iCloud account is signed out, network is down, or container quota is exceeded. | Surface to the user; iCloud sync is required to be opt-in anyway. |

## Reading `details.path`

`error.details.path` is a JSONPath-style locator into the request body. Examples:

- `path: "$"` — the whole payload (commonly seen on `DFQL_INVALID`).
- `path: "filters.status"` — the offending filter clause.
- `path: "select"` — a bad select projection.
- `path: "steps[3].mutation.record.title"` — a transaction step's record field.

This is the fastest way to triage validation errors without re-reading the entire request.

## Pattern: handling errors in the client

```typescript
const result = await client.table("tasks").mutate({
  operation: "insert",
  record: { title: "" },
});

if (!result.ok) {
  switch (result.error.code) {
    case "DFQL_INVALID":
      showFieldError(result.error.details?.path, result.error.message);
      break;
    case "FORBIDDEN":
      navigate("/login");
      break;
    case "TRANSPORT_ERROR":
      queueForRetry(result);
      break;
    default:
      showToast(`Unexpected error: ${result.error.code}`);
  }
}
```

Always switch on `code`. Never parse `message`; it's human-readable and may change between versions.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Events Reference

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/events
Description: Plugin hook events fired during query, mutation, and sync execution.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

DataFn plugins receive structured events. The same event shape is used on client and server so the same hook can run in both places.

## DatafnEvent

```typescript
type DatafnEvent =
  | "beforeQuery"  | "afterQuery"
  | "beforeMutation" | "afterMutation"
  | "beforeTransact" | "afterTransact"
  | "beforeSync" | "afterSync";
```

| Event | Fires when | Mutating? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `beforeQuery` | A `/datafn/query` (or local read) is about to execute | yes — return a modified query to alter the request |
| `afterQuery` | A query finished | yes — return a modified result set |
| `beforeMutation` | A `/datafn/mutation` (or local write) is about to execute | yes — return a modified mutation or `{ abort: { code, message } }` |
| `afterMutation` | A mutation finished | no — observation only |
| `beforeTransact` | A `/datafn/transact` is about to execute | yes — modify steps |
| `afterTransact` | A transaction finished | no |
| `beforeSync` | A sync push or pull is about to execute | yes — see hook semantics below |
| `afterSync` | A sync round-trip finished | no |

## DatafnEventFilter

Plugins may scope their hooks to specific resources or operations:

```typescript
type DatafnEventFilter = {
  resource?: string | string[];
  operation?: DfqlOperation | DfqlOperation[];
};
```

`undefined` matches everything.

## DatafnHookContext

The argument passed to each hook:

```typescript
type DatafnHookContext = {
  event: DatafnEvent;
  resource?: string;
  payload: unknown; // event-specific (DfqlQuery, DfqlMutation, …)
  ctx?: unknown;    // server request context (e.g. ctx.user)
  meta?: Record<string, unknown>;
};
```

## Defining a plugin

```typescript
import type { DatafnPlugin } from "@datafn/core";

export const myPlugin: DatafnPlugin = {
  name: "log-mutations",
  hooks: [
    {
      event: "beforeMutation",
      filter: { resource: ["tasks", "projects"] },
      handler: async (ctx) => {
        console.log("mutation", ctx.payload);
        return undefined; // pass through unchanged
      },
    },
    {
      event: "afterMutation",
      handler: async (ctx) => {
        // observation only; don't return a value
        await metrics.record("mutation", { resource: ctx.resource });
      },
    },
  ],
};
```

Register on the server via `plugins: [myPlugin]` in `createDatafnServer`, and on the client via `plugins: [myPlugin]` in `createDatafnClient`.

## Return values

### before* hooks

A before-hook may return:

- `undefined` → pass through unchanged.
- A modified payload of the same shape → the modified value replaces the original (for example a `beforeQuery` may extend `filters`).
- `{ abort: { code: DatafnErrorCode; message: string; details?: unknown } }` → abort execution and return that error to the caller.

Multiple before-hooks are run in registration order; the first abort short-circuits the rest.

### after* hooks

After-hooks are observation only. Return value is ignored. Throwing aborts subsequent after-hooks but does **not** roll back the executed mutation. Use throwing only to fail-fast in development.

## Common patterns

### Field redaction

```typescript
{
  event: "afterQuery",
  filter: { resource: "users" },
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const result = ctx.payload as { data: any[] };
    return {
      ...result,
      data: result.data.map((row) => {
        if (ctx.ctx?.user?.role !== "admin") delete row.email;
        return row;
      }),
    };
  },
}
```

### Computed timestamps

```typescript
{
  event: "beforeMutation",
  filter: { resource: "tasks", operation: ["insert", "merge"] },
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const mut = ctx.payload as DfqlMutation;
    return {
      ...mut,
      record: { ...mut.record, dueDateMs: new Date(mut.record.dueDate as string).getTime() },
    };
  },
}
```

### Outbound webhooks

```typescript
{
  event: "afterMutation",
  filter: { resource: "orders" },
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    await sendWebhook("https://hooks.example.com/orders", ctx.payload);
  },
}
```

### Hard abort

```typescript
{
  event: "beforeMutation",
  filter: { resource: "tasks" },
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const mut = ctx.payload as DfqlMutation;
    if (mut.operation === "delete" && !ctx.ctx?.user?.isAdmin) {
      return { abort: { code: "FORBIDDEN", message: "Only admins can delete tasks" } };
    }
  },
}
```

See [Plugins → Custom Plugins](/docs/documentation/plugins/custom-plugins) for narrative coverage.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### HTTP Routes Reference

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/routes
Description: Canonical reference for every route exposed by the DataFn server: method, path, request shape, response shape, and error codes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every DataFn server, regardless of host framework, exposes the same set of HTTP routes under the `/datafn/*` prefix. They share a single response envelope:

```typescript
// Success
{ "ok": true,  "result": <route-specific> }
// Error
{ "ok": false, "error": { "code": "<DatafnErrorCode>", "message": "...", "details": { "path": "..." } } }
```

POST endpoints accept `application/json`. The Python server returns the same envelope.

For narrative documentation and a per-framework walkthrough, see [Server Routes](/docs/documentation/server/routes).

## GET /datafn/status

Health check and server metadata. TypeScript server only (Python parity is on the roadmap).

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Method / Path** | `GET /datafn/status` |
| **Auth** | optional — checked via `authorize(ctx, "status", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `INTERNAL` on database failure |

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "result": {
    "schemaHash": "sha256:abc123...",
    "capabilities": ["dfql.query", "dfql.mutation", "dfql.transact", "dfql.sync", "dfql.seed"],
    "limits": { "maxLimit": 100, "maxTransactSteps": 100, "maxPayloadBytes": 5242880 },
    "serverTimeMs": 1709251200000
  }
}
```

`serverTimeMs` is rounded to the nearest minute to prevent fingerprinting.

## POST /datafn/query

Execute one or many DFQL queries.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body (single)** | `DfqlQuery` |
| **Body (batch)** | `DfqlQuery[]` (max `limits.maxBatchSize`) |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "query", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `DFQL_INVALID`, `DFQL_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE`, `DFQL_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `FORBIDDEN` |

Single response: `{ data: <Record[]>, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }`
Batch response: `Array<{ data: <Record[]>, hasMore: boolean }>` aligned to the request order.

Implicit filtering:

- `trash` capability: `metadata.includeTrashed === false` (default) excludes trashed rows.
- `archivable` capability: `metadata.includeArchived === false` (default) excludes archived rows.
- `shareable` capability with `defaultVisibility: "private"`: only owned + explicitly-shared rows are returned.

## POST /datafn/mutation

Execute one or many DFQL mutations.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body (single)** | `DfqlMutation` |
| **Body (batch)** | `DfqlMutation[]` (max `limits.maxBatchSize`) |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "mutation", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `DFQL_INVALID`, `DFQL_UNKNOWN_RESOURCE`, `DFQL_UNKNOWN_FIELD`, `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED`, `NOT_FOUND`, `CONFLICT`, `FORBIDDEN`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` |

Valid `operation` values:

- Core: `insert`, `merge`, `replace`, `delete`
- Capability: `trash`, `restore`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `share`, `unshare`
- Relation: `relate`, `modifyRelation`, `unrelate`

Single response: `{ id: string, serverSeq: number }`.

Replay safety: `clientId` + `mutationId` enables idempotency. A replay returns the cached result without re-executing.

## POST /datafn/transact

Execute multiple steps atomically.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ steps: Array<{ type?: "query" \| "mutation"; query?: DfqlQuery; mutation?: DfqlMutation }> }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "transact", payload)` |
| **Errors** | Every error from `/datafn/query` and `/datafn/mutation`; on failure of any step, prior mutations roll back and the response includes `TRANSACTION_ROLLED_BACK` |

Response: `{ results: Array<{ id?: string; serverSeq?: number; data?: Record[] }> }` aligned to step order.

Bounded by `limits.maxTransactSteps` (default 100).

## POST /datafn/seed

Initialize a dataset for a client. Idempotent.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ clientId: string }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "seed", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `INTERNAL` |
| **Response** | `{ ok: true }` |

## POST /datafn/clone

Initial sync. Returns every visible record plus per-resource cursors.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ clientId: string; tables?: string[]; includeJoins?: boolean }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "clone", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `FORBIDDEN`, `INTERNAL` |

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "data": { "<resource>": [<Record>...] },
  "cursors": { "<resource>": "42" },
  "joins": { },
  "next": { "<resource>": null }
}
```

`next` is non-null when results are paginated; pass it back to continue cloning.

## POST /datafn/pull

Incremental sync since a cursor.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ clientId: string; cursors: Record<string,string>; includeJoins?: boolean; limit?: number }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "pull", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `FORBIDDEN`, `INTERNAL`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (limit above `limits.maxPullLimit`) |

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "records": { "<resource>": [<Record>...] },
  "merged":  { "<resource>": [<Record>...] },
  "deleted": { "<resource>": [<id>...] },
  "joins":   { "<from>.<rel>.<to>": { "upsert": [], "delete": [] } },
  "cursors": { "<resource>": "47" },
  "hasMore": false
}
```

When `hasMore` is true the client should pull again with the returned cursors.

## POST /datafn/push

Push offline mutations.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ clientId: string; mutations: DfqlMutation[] }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "push", payload)` |
| **Errors** | Same as `/datafn/mutation`; bulk results in `errors` array |

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "applied": ["mut_001", "mut_002"],
  "errors":  [{ "mutationId": "mut_003", "code": "CONFLICT", "message": "..." }],
  "cursor":  "47",
  "cursorBefore": "44",
  "cursors": { "<resource>": "47" }
}
```

After a successful push, connected WebSocket clients in the same namespace receive a cursor notification.

## POST /datafn/reconcile

Resolve client/server state after long offline windows. TypeScript server only.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ clientId: string; resources?: string[]; includeJoins?: boolean }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "reconcile", payload)` |
| **Response** | `{ counts: { <resource>: number }, joinCounts: {}, latestCursor: string }` |

## POST /datafn/search

Cross-resource search via the configured `SearchProvider`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Body** | `{ query: string; resources?: string[]; limit?: number }` |
| **Auth** | `authorize(ctx, "search", payload)` |
| **Errors** | `DFQL_UNSUPPORTED` if no provider is configured, `INTERNAL` |
| **Response** | `{ results: Array<{ resource: string; id: string; score: number; snippet?: string }> }` |

## POST /datafn/rest/&lt;resource&gt;/&lt;id?&gt;

Auto-generated REST surface for each resource. Enabled via `rest: true` in `createDatafnServer`.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **GET /datafn/rest/`<resource>`** | List records |
| **GET /datafn/rest/`<resource>`/`<id>`** | Read by id |
| **POST /datafn/rest/`<resource>`** | Create |
| **PATCH /datafn/rest/`<resource>`/`<id>`** | Merge |
| **PUT /datafn/rest/`<resource>`/`<id>`** | Replace |
| **DELETE /datafn/rest/`<resource>`/`<id>`** | Delete |

REST translates to DFQL internally, so the same error codes and capability semantics apply.

## WS /datafn/ws

WebSocket endpoint for live cursor notifications. After a successful push, namespaced clients receive `{ type: "cursor", cursors: { <resource>: string } }` so they can issue a follow-up `/datafn/pull` and update their local store.

See [WebSockets](/docs/documentation/server/websockets) for the full protocol.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Server Configuration

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/config
Description: Full configuration reference for createDatafnServer.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## DatafnServerConfig\<TContext\>

Complete configuration for `createDatafnServer`.

```typescript
interface DatafnServerConfig<TContext = any> {
  /** Required. DataFn schema (validated at startup). */
  schema: DatafnSchema;

  /** Database adapter for persistence. */
  db?: Adapter;

  /** Client-side and server-side plugins. */
  plugins?: DatafnPlugin[];

  /** Authorization callback. Called after JSON parsing, before execution. */
  authorize?: (
    ctx: TContext,
    action: "status" | "query" | "mutation" | "transact"
      | "seed" | "clone" | "pull" | "push" | "reconcile",
    payload: unknown,
  ) => Promise<boolean> | boolean;

  /** Server-side limits. */
  limits?: {
    maxLimit?: number;              // Default: 100
    maxTransactSteps?: number;
    maxPayloadBytes?: number;       // Default: 5MB
    maxPullLimit?: number;          // Default: 1000
    maxSelectTokens?: number;       // Default: 50
    maxFilterKeysPerLevel?: number; // Default: 20
    maxSortFields?: number;         // Default: 10
    maxAggregations?: number;       // Default: 20
    maxIdLength?: number;           // Default: 255
    maxBatchSize?: number;          // Default: 500
    maxBatchQueryConcurrency?: number; // Default: 20
  };

  /** Debug mode for verbose error messages. Default: true in non-production. */
  debug?: boolean;

  /** Allow queries on resources without authorization policy. Default: false. */
  allowUnknownResources?: boolean;

  /** Custom server time provider (for testing). */
  getServerTime?: () => number;

  /** Enable REST endpoint generation. Default: false. */
  rest?: boolean;

  /** Namespace provider for data isolation. */
  namespaceProvider?: {
    getNamespace: (ctx: TContext) => string | Promise<string>;
    getActorId?: (ctx: TContext) => string | Promise<string>;
  };

  /** Redis adapter for atomic operations. */
  redis?: RedisAdapter;

  /** KV store adapter for simple key-value operations. */
  kvStore?: KVStoreAdapter;

  /** Database mapping: which database to use for each feature. */
  dbMapping?: DbMapping;

  /** Row-level namespace isolation. false to disable, object to configure. */
  rowLevelNamespace?: false | RowLevelNamespaceConfig;

  /** Data retention configuration. */
  retention?: RetentionConfig;

  /** Rate limiting configuration. */
  rateLimit?: RateLimitConfig<TContext>;

  /** Observability (timing events). */
  observability?: ObservabilityConfig;

  /** WebSocket limits and heartbeat. */
  ws?: WsManagerConfig;

  /** Graceful shutdown drain timeout in ms. Default: 10000. */
  shutdownTimeoutMs?: number;

  /** Pluggable logger. Default: console-based. */
  logger?: DatafnLogger;
}
```

## RetentionConfig

```typescript
interface RetentionConfig {
  /** Days to retain change log entries. Default: unlimited. */
  changeLogDays?: number;
  /** Days to retain idempotency records. Default: unlimited. */
  idempotencyDays?: number;
  /** Run pruning on server startup. Default: false. */
  pruneOnStartup?: boolean;
  /** Interval in ms for periodic pruning. Minimum: 60000. */
  pruneIntervalMs?: number;
}
```

## RateLimitConfig\<TContext\>

```typescript
interface RateLimitConfig<TContext = any> {
  /** Enable rate limiting. Default: false. */
  enabled: boolean;
  /** Max requests per window per client. Default: 100. */
  maxRequests?: number;
  /** Window duration in seconds. Default: 60. */
  windowSeconds?: number;
  /** Per-endpoint overrides. */
  endpoints?: Partial<Record<
    "query" | "mutation" | "transact" | "push" | "pull" | "clone" | "reconcile" | "seed",
    { maxRequests: number; windowSeconds: number }
  >>;
  /** Key extractor for identifying clients. */
  keyExtractor?: (ctx: TContext) => string | Promise<string>;
}
```

## ObservabilityConfig

```typescript
interface ObservabilityConfig {
  /** Emit execution timing events. Default: false. */
  timing?: boolean;
  /** Custom timing event handler. Default: console.debug. */
  onTiming?: (event: ExecutionTimingEvent) => void;
}
```

## WsManagerConfig

```typescript
interface WsManagerConfig {
  /** Max total WS connections. Default: 10000. */
  maxConnections?: number;
  /** Max connections per namespace. Default: 100. */
  maxConnectionsPerNamespace?: number;
  /** Heartbeat ping interval in ms. Default: 30000. */
  heartbeatIntervalMs?: number;
  /** Max time to wait for pong. Default: 10000. */
  heartbeatTimeoutMs?: number;
}
```

## Defaults Summary

| Option | Default |
|---|---|
| `limits.maxLimit` | 100 |
| `limits.maxPayloadBytes` | 5,242,880 (5 MB) |
| `limits.maxPullLimit` | 1000 |
| `limits.maxSelectTokens` | 50 |
| `limits.maxFilterKeysPerLevel` | 20 |
| `limits.maxSortFields` | 10 |
| `limits.maxAggregations` | 20 |

| `debug` | `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` |

| `ws.maxConnections` | 10000 |
| `ws.maxConnectionsPerNamespace` | 100 |
| `ws.heartbeatIntervalMs` | 30000 |
| `ws.heartbeatTimeoutMs` | 10000 |



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Execution Engine

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/execution
Description: Query and mutation execution internals.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## DataStore Interface

The execution engine operates through a `DataStore` abstraction. Two implementations are provided:

### DbDataStore

Wraps a database adapter (`@superfunctions/db` `Adapter`) for persistent storage. All operations pass through the adapter's query builder.

### MemoryStore

In-memory implementation using `Map<string, Map<string, Record>>`. Used for testing and local-only mode.

## Query Execution

### Planning and Classification

Queries are classified by type to optimize execution:

| Classification | Condition | Strategy |
|---|---|---|
| **Find by ID** | `filter.id.$eq` present | Direct record lookup. |
| **Pushdown** | Database adapter available | Translate DFQL to SQL and execute at the database level. |
| **Memory scan** | No adapter or pushdown not possible | Load all records, apply filters in-memory. |

### Pushdown Query Execution

When a database adapter is available, the query engine pushes as much work as possible to the database:

- **Filters** -- translated to SQL WHERE clauses.
- **Sort** -- translated to SQL ORDER BY.
- **Limit/Cursor** -- translated to SQL LIMIT/OFFSET or keyset pagination.
- **Aggregations** -- translated to SQL aggregate functions (COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX).

Fields and operators not supported by pushdown fall back to in-memory evaluation after the database query returns.

## Mutation Execution

### Flow

1. **Guard evaluation** -- check field-level constraints (required, readonly, enum, min/max, pattern, unique).
2. **Relation handling** -- for mutations with relation payloads, normalize and execute join table operations.
3. **Store operation** -- execute the create/update/delete against the data store.
4. **Change tracking** -- record the mutation in the `__datafn_changes` internal table with a monotonic sequence number.

Capability-enabled operations (`trash`, `restore`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `share`, `unshare`) flow through the same execution path with additional capability checks and field injection/stripping rules.

### Guard Store

Validates field constraints at mutation time:

- **Required** -- non-null check on insert.
- **Readonly** -- reject updates to readonly fields.
- **Unique** -- check for existing records with the same value (scoped to namespace).
- **Enum** -- value must be in the allowed set.
- **Min/Max** -- numeric range validation.
- **MinLength/MaxLength** -- string length validation.
- **Pattern** -- regex validation.

## Change Tracking

The `ChangeTrackingService` records every mutation as a change entry:

```typescript
{
  serverSeq: number;    // Monotonic sequence
  resource: string;
  action: "insert" | "merge" | "replace" | "delete";
  recordId: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
  timestamp: number;
  namespace: string;
}
```

Changes are stored in the `__datafn_changes` internal table and queried by the pull handler.

## Sequence Store

Generates monotonic sequence numbers for change tracking. Multiple backends:

| Implementation | Backend | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `RedisSequenceStore` | Redis | Atomic `INCR` on a Redis key. Highest throughput. |
| `KVSequenceStore` | KV Store | `incr()` on a KV key. |
| `DatabaseSequenceStore` | Database | Row-level locking with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`. |
| Combined sequence chain | Primary + database chain | Coordinates primary sequence allocation with database continuity. |

The `createSequenceStore` factory selects the implementation based on `dbMapping.serverseq`:

```typescript
const store = createSequenceStore({
  db,
  redis,
  kvStore,
  dbMapping: { serverseq: "redis" },
});
```

## Internal Tables

The execution engine manages two internal tables:

| Table | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `__datafn_changes` | Change tracking entries for sync pull. |
| `__datafn_idempotency` | Idempotency records for mutation deduplication. |

These tables are automatically created by the database adapter and are transparent to application code.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Middleware

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/middleware
Description: Rate limiting and timing middleware reference.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Rate Limiting

### RateLimiter Interface

```typescript
interface RateLimiter {
  check(
    key: string,
    maxRequests: number,
    windowSeconds: number,
  ): Promise<{ allowed: boolean; remaining: number }>;
}
```

### RedisRateLimiter

Redis-backed rate limiter using atomic `INCR` with TTL. Key format: `ratelimit:{endpoint}:{clientKey}:{windowId}`.

```typescript
class RedisRateLimiter implements RateLimiter {
  constructor(redis: RedisAdapter);
}
```

Uses an atomic Lua script when the Redis client supports `eval()`:

```lua
local c = redis.call('incr', KEYS[1])
if c == 1 then redis.call('expire', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]) end
return c
```

Falls back to non-atomic `INCR` + `EXPIRE` for clients that do not support `eval`.

### MemoryRateLimiter

In-memory sliding window limiter. Single-process only.

```typescript
class MemoryRateLimiter implements RateLimiter {
  constructor(sweepIntervalMs?: number); // Default: 60000
  destroy(): void;
}
```

Uses a `Map<string, { count, resetAt }>` with periodic sweep to remove expired entries. Call `destroy()` on shutdown to stop the sweep timer and allow the process to exit.

### Rate Limit Middleware

Applied **before** JSON parsing and authorization. Returns `null` if the request is allowed, or a `429` response with `Retry-After` header if rate-limited.

```typescript
function createRateLimitMiddleware(config: {
  limiter: RateLimiter;
  maxRequests: number;
  windowSeconds: number;
  endpoints?: Partial<Record<string, { maxRequests: number; windowSeconds: number }>>;
  keyExtractor: (ctx: any) => string | Promise<string>;
}): (endpoint: string, ctx: any) => Promise<Response | null>;
```

## Execution Timing

### ExecutionTimer

Tracks named execution phases sequentially.

```typescript
class ExecutionTimer {
  /** Start a named phase. Ends any in-progress phase. */
  startPhase(name: string): void;

  /** End the current phase. */
  endPhase(): void;

  /** Build the final timing event. */
  build(endpoint: string, resource?: string, operation?: string): ExecutionTimingEvent;
}
```

### ExecutionTimingEvent

```typescript
interface ExecutionTimingEvent {
  endpoint: string;
  resource?: string;
  operation?: string;
  phases: Record<string, number>; // phase name -> duration ms
  totalMs: number;
  timestamp: string; // ISO 8601
}
```

### TimingEmitter

Created from `ObservabilityConfig`. Returns `null` if timing is disabled (no runtime overhead). Custom `onTiming` handler errors are caught and logged.

```typescript
function createTimingEmitter(config?: {
  timing?: boolean;
  onTiming?: (event: ExecutionTimingEvent) => void;
}, logger?: DatafnLogger): TimingEmitter | null;
```

Usage in route handlers:

```typescript
const timer = new ExecutionTimer();
timer.startPhase("validate");
// ... validation ...
timer.startPhase("execute");
// ... execution ...
const event = timer.build("query", "todos");
timingEmitter?.(event);
```



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### Route Handlers

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/routes
Description: Server route lifecycle and capability-aware execution notes.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Overview

Route handlers share a common lifecycle:

1. parse/validate body,
2. authorize,
3. normalize capability fields,
4. execute,
5. return envelope.

## Query Handler (`POST /datafn/query`)

- validates schema-bounded query shape,
- resolves shareable access constraints,
- injects capability auto-filters (`trash`/`archivable` defaults),
- executes query plan (pushdown or in-memory/materialized),
- runs after-query hooks.

## Mutation Handler (`POST /datafn/mutation`)

- validates mutation structure and operation,
- validates capability gating for operation (`trash`, `archive`, `share`, etc.),
- strips readonly capability-managed fields from records before execution,
- executes mutation logic with idempotency + change tracking,
- runs hooks and emits sync-visible changes.

Supported operations include:

- core: `insert`, `merge`, `replace`, `delete`
- capability: `trash`, `restore`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `share`, `unshare`
- relation: `relate`, `modifyRelation`, `unrelate`

## Transact Handler (`POST /datafn/transact`)

Executes query/mutation steps in transaction scope and returns ordered step results. Validation and capability enforcement apply to mutation steps the same way as direct mutation routes.

## Sync Handlers

### Clone (`POST /datafn/clone`)

Returns full resource snapshots (optionally paginated) for hydration.

### Pull (`POST /datafn/pull`)

Returns ordered changes after cursor, bounded by configured limits.

### Push (`POST /datafn/push`)

Processes mutation batches from client changelog.

Important parity rule: push path applies the same capability readonly stripping and capability operation semantics as direct mutation path.

### Reconcile (`POST /datafn/reconcile`)

Compares client and server resource state summaries to determine re-clone requirements.

## Seed Handler (`POST /datafn/seed`)

Applies initial data payloads, idempotently scoped to namespace.



--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
### WebSocket Manager

URL: https://datafn.21n.co/docs/reference/server/websocket
Description: WebSocket manager reference.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## WebSocketManager

Manages WebSocket connections for real-time sync notifications. Connections are tracked per-namespace for efficient broadcast.

```typescript
class WebSocketManager {
  constructor(config?: WsManagerConfig, logger?: DatafnLogger);

  addClient(client: WebSocketClient, authContext: WsAuthContext): boolean;
  removeClient(client: WebSocketClient): void;
  handleMessage(client: WebSocketClient, data: string): void;
  handlePong(client: WebSocketClient): void;
  broadcastCursor(cursor: string, namespace: string): void;
  close(): void;
  destroy(): void;
}
```

## WebSocketClient Interface

```typescript
interface WebSocketClient {
  send(data: string): void;
  close?(code?: number, reason?: string): void;
  ping?(): void;
}
```

## WsAuthContext

```typescript
interface WsAuthContext {
  namespace: string;
}
```

The namespace is **server-derived** from the `namespaceProvider`. Client-supplied namespace values in messages are ignored.

## addClient

Registers a client after authentication. Returns `false` if connection limits are exceeded.

**Security requirements:**
- The caller must reject unauthenticated connections with close code `4401` before calling `addClient`.
- The namespace in `authContext` is locked at connection time and cannot be changed.

**Connection limits:**
- Global limit: `maxConnections` (default: 10,000).
- Per-namespace limit: `maxConnectionsPerNamespace` (default: 100).
- Rejected connections receive close code `4503`.

## removeClient

Removes a client from tracking. Called on disconnect or when a heartbeat times out.

## handleMessage

Processes incoming WebSocket messages. Currently handles the `hello` message type for client registration. The namespace field in hello messages is ignored (server-derived only).

## handlePong

Called by the WebSocket transport when a native pong frame is received. Clears the pending-pong marker so the connection is not timed out by the heartbeat.

## broadcastCursor

Sends a cursor update to all clients in a namespace. Complexity is O(clients in namespace). Failed sends result in client removal.

```typescript
// Message format
{ "type": "cursor", "cursor": "42" }
```

## Heartbeat

The heartbeat starts lazily when the first client connects. It pings all clients at `heartbeatIntervalMs` (default: 30s). Clients that do not respond with a pong within `heartbeatTimeoutMs` (default: 10s) are closed with code `1001`.

## Close Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `4401` | Unauthorized (caller should send before `addClient`). |
| `4503` | Connection limit exceeded. |
| `1001` | Going away (graceful shutdown or heartbeat timeout). |

## Graceful Shutdown

`close()` stops the heartbeat timer, sends close code `1001` ("Going Away") to all connected clients, and clears all internal state. Called automatically by `DatafnServer.close()`.
